ideas.description: On the E026 tip (commit da18628: compiled batched Muon, 2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 px, 8.0 epochs), change only the Newton-Schulz iteration count in the compiled Muon update from 3 to 4. Keep the quintic coefficients (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315), bf16, batching and everything else. Re-warm the compiled update in build for every filter shape. E031 showed the opposite direction (3 -> 2) costs 1.82 pp for -2.3% time. So orthogonalization quality is an accuracy knob, and one more iteration may buy margin at ~0.32 ms/step. Log per-seed accuracy and per-trial train time.
ideas.expected: Time +2 to +2.6% (about 5.62-5.65 s; one NS iteration measured at ~0.124 s per trial in E031). Accuracy 0.756-0.760, i.e. +0.1 to +0.5 pp over the 0.7554 tip estimate. If the gain is >=0.3 pp (3-seed mean >=0.7585), this beats every epoch exchange rate (0.035-0.08 pp per 1%). The next step then stacks it on the 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 near-miss (E029: -0.27 s for -0.31 pp), for about 5.36 s at ~0.755. If the gain is <0.15 pp, 3 iterations are already saturated, and NS work is closed in both directions.

ideas.description: On the E026 tip, keep 3 Newton-Schulz iterations but replace the fixed quintic coefficients with per-iteration optimal coefficients for a 3-step schedule. Compute them offline with the Polar Express procedure (arXiv 2505.16932): minimax-optimal odd quintics for the singular-value interval [l, 1] with l about 1e-3, and a small safety factor (~1.01) for bf16. Hard-code them as constants. Before the scored run, do an untimed check that the singular values of a random 384x3456 bf16 matrix land closer to 1 (report min/max) than with the fixed coefficients. Same FLOPs, so time should be unchanged. Re-warm the compiled update in build.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%, ~5.50 s). Accuracy +0.0 to +0.5 pp over the 0.7554 estimate, because the orthogonalization is better at equal cost (E031: quality matters by ~1.8 pp per iteration). A 3-seed mean >=0.7575 makes it the new tip with free margin to spend on a 3rd 16 px epoch. A result at or below 0.7554 means the fixed coefficients are already good enough at 3 steps, and only the iteration count (the NS-4 idea) remains.

ideas.description: On the E026 tip, change only the Muon learning rate from 0.24 to 0.20 (momentum 0.6, Nesterov, same schedule shape; the LR is already a 0-d GPU tensor, so nothing recompiles). Both independently tuned public Muon recipes use 0.205-0.2255. E030 showed momentum is flat between 0.5 and 0.6, so lr is the one Muon knob left untested (the dropped I039 never ran).
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.2 to +0.4 pp vs 0.7554. H7.1.2 is supported at >=0.7575. A result of <=0.7535 suggests 0.24 is at or below the optimum, so a probe at 0.28 is warranted. Anything in between is noise, and the Muon hyperparameters are closed.

ideas.description: On the E026 tip, change only how often the Muon-managed conv filters are renormalized: every 2 + int(15*progress) steps instead of every step (hiverge/Fable style). Do it inside the compiled update with a 0-d bool/int tensor flag (torch.where-gated, or two warmed-up variants selected on the host) so nothing recompiles in timed code. Warm up both paths in build. Everything else is unchanged. Before scoring, log per-step update time with CUDA events in an untimed run, to separate the renorm cost from NS.
ideas.expected: Time -0.5 to -2% (about 5.39-5.47 s). Renorm is a norm plus a scale over 9 filters, probably ~0.05-0.15 ms/step, so the >=1.5% that H7.2.1 predicts is optimistic. Accuracy within ±0.25 pp of 0.7554. If time falls by <0.7%, renorm is not a meaningful part of the Muon overhead, and what remains is NS matmuls plus momentum traffic, which only batch size can cut.

ideas.description: Determinism probe on the E026 tip, with no change to the math or hyperparameters. Compile the Muon update with mode='default' instead of 'max-autotune-no-cudagraphs', and set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=False with cudnn.deterministic=True for all train/eval shapes. Keep the net's own compile as is. Warm everything up in build. Run the scored evaluation, then rerun seed 0 once in an untimed side script through the benchmark's trial code and compare per-seed accuracy bit for bit.
ideas.expected: Time +0 to +1.5% (5.50-5.58 s). Accuracy within noise of 0.7554. If the seed-0 repeat is bit-identical, run-to-run noise is gone. Seed-paired comparisons then become possible, which roughly halves the noise on recipe differences (~0.2 pp sd now). The setting should become the default whenever its cost is <=0.5%. If the repeat still differs, the non-determinism comes from the net's own max-autotune picks for the new 16/24 px shapes or from atomics in the backward pass, and H4.3 is refuted.

ideas.description: On the E026 tip, change only label smoothing from 0.3 to 0.2. Change nothing else. LS 0.3 was tuned under SGD (E009). Muon fits faster, and tuned public Muon recipes use much lower LS (0.09), so the Muon tip may be over-regularized.
ideas.expected: Time unchanged (±0.5%). Accuracy -0.3 to +0.4 pp vs 0.7554. H6.3.1 is supported at >=0.7575, which would give free slack for the E029 3@16 schedule. A result of <=0.7535 confirms LS 0.3 is optimal under Muon too, and zero-cost loss tuning is closed for good.

ideas.description: On the E026 tip, raise the batch size from 1024 to 1536 (2@16 + 2@24 + 4@32 px, still 8.0 epochs). Scale the SGD param groups (BN/bias/head) by the E010 kilostep rule. Keep Muon lr 0.24 and momentum 0.6. Rescale the LR warmup/decay, EMA and lookahead schedules to the new step count (~256 steps). Compile and warm up the 1536-batch shapes at 16/24/32 px in build. The remaining Muon cost is per step (~1 ms), so a third fewer steps cuts it directly. E022 showed Muon tolerates large batches (-0.25 pp at bs 2000).
ideas.expected: Time -2 to -3.5% (about 5.31-5.39 s): ~128 fewer steps x ~1 ms of Muon, plus per-step SGD/launch costs in the small-map phases. Accuracy -0.05 to -0.35 pp (0.752-0.755). If accuracy is >=0.753 with time <=5.40 s, it is the new tip. A loss of >=0.4 pp means Muon's batch tolerance shrinks at short schedules, so per-step overhead should be attacked inside the update instead.

structured_output.summary: I added 7 ideas, for 8 queued in total including I040. No queued idea was dropped, because I040's hypothesis H2.4.1 is still open. The new ideas mostly go after accuracy first: the tip is about 0.7554 against a 0.753 bar, so it has only ~0.25 pp of real margin. The top idea follows from E031: going from 3 to 2 Newton-Schulz iterations cost 1.8 pp, so a 4th iteration (~+2.3% time) may buy a few tenths of a pp more cheaply than any change to the epoch schedule. A related idea keeps 3 iterations at equal cost but uses Polar Express per-iteration coefficients. Two untested zero-cost knobs are also queued: Muon lr 0.20 (the dropped I039 never ran) and label smoothing 0.2 under Muon. Any margin they buy would pay for the E029 3@16 + 1@24 + 4@32 near-miss (-0.27 s). For Muon overhead there are two ideas: periodic weight renormalization, and bs 1536 to cut the step count. A determinism probe (Muon compiled with mode='default', cuDNN algorithm choice pinned) would make seed-paired comparisons possible, roughly halving the noise on recipe differences. H2.10.1 (reinvesting the low-res savings in a longer 32 px tail) waits for the running I038 (4@16 + 4@32). H7.1.1 is effectively answered by E030: momentum 0.5 brought no gain.
